name: ADG707BRUZ-REEL7
title: 2.5 Ω CMOS 16-to-1 and differential 8-to-1 multiplexers, 1.8 V to 5.5 V or ±2.5 V
summary: The ADG706 routes one of 16 inputs to a single output under a 4-bit address; the ADG707 routes one of eight input pairs to a differential output pair under a 3-bit address. Both run from one supply of 1.8 V to 5.5 V or from ±2.5 V, pass signals rail to rail in either direction with about 2.5 Ω ON resistance, and have an active-high enable: with EN low every switch is off. Channels break before they make. Both come in a 28-lead TSSOP.
key_figures: 1.8 V to 5.5 V single, ±2.5 V dual

circuits.title: Test circuit 1: ON resistance
circuits.description: A current IDS is forced through one closed switch from S to D while VS sets the source voltage; the voltage V1 across the switch divided by IDS gives RON.

circuits.title: Test circuit 2: IS (OFF)
circuits.description: EN is held at 0.8 V so every switch is off. S1 is driven from VS through an ammeter that reads its leakage; the other sources and D are tied together at VD.

circuits.title: Test circuit 3: ID (OFF)
circuits.description: EN at 0.8 V turns every switch off. All sources sit at VS; D is held at VD through an ammeter that reads the drain leakage.

circuits.title: Test circuit 4: ID (ON)
circuits.description: EN at 2.4 V turns the addressed switch on. The sources sit at VS and D at VD through an ammeter, which reads the leakage of the closed channel.

circuits.title: Test circuit 5: switching time of multiplexer, tTRANSITION
circuits.description: All four address lines are driven together by a 0 V to 3 V pulse terminated in 50 Ω, so the part steps between channel 1 and channel 16. S1 sits at VS1, S16 at VS16, the rest are grounded, and D drives 300 Ω parallel with 35 pF. tTRANSITION runs from the 50% point of the address edge to the 90% point of the output. The ADG707 is measured with the same connections.
notes: Misprint: the grounded group S1 THRU S15 should read S2 THRU S15.

circuits.title: Test circuit 6: break-before-make delay, tOPEN
circuits.description: The address lines step together from a 50 Ω terminated 0 V to 3 V pulse. S1 and S16 are both at VS, so the output dips only while neither switch is on; the time between the 80% points of that dip is tOPEN. D drives 300 Ω parallel with 35 pF. The ADG707 is measured with the same connections.
notes: Misprint: the grounded group S1 THRU S15 should read S2 THRU S15.

circuits.title: Test circuit 7: enable delay, tON (EN), tOFF (EN)
circuits.description: The address lines are grounded, selecting channel 1, with S1 at VS and S2 to S16 grounded. EN is driven by a 0 V to 3 V pulse terminated in 50 Ω; D drives 300 Ω parallel with 35 pF. The delays run from the 50% point of the EN edge to 90% of the final output. The ADG707 is measured with the same connections.

circuits.title: Test circuit 8: charge injection
circuits.description: The address lines are grounded. S is fed from VS through RS, D is loaded by 1 nF only, and EN is pulsed between 0 V and 3 V. The step ΔVOUT left on the capacitor times CL gives the injected charge. The ADG707 is measured with the same connections.

circuits.title: Test circuit 9: OFF isolation and bandwidth
circuits.description: The address lines are grounded. S1 to S16 are tied together and fed from a signal source VS through 50 Ω and a selector contact; D is loaded with 50 Ω. With EN grounded every switch is off and 20 log10(VOUT/VS) is the OFF isolation; with EN at 2.4 V the ratio of VOUT with and without the switch gives insertion loss and bandwidth. The ADG707 is measured with similar connections.
notes: Insertion loss is 20 log10 of the ratio between VOUT measured through the switch and VOUT measured with the switch taken out.
EN goes to 2.4 V for the bandwidth measurement.

circuits.title: Test circuit 10: channel-to-channel crosstalk
circuits.description: The address lines are grounded and EN is at 2.4 V, so S1 is connected to D, which is loaded by 50 Ω; S1 is terminated to ground by 50 Ω. The off channels S2 to S16 are tied together and driven from a source VS through 50 Ω and a selector contact; 20 log10(VOUT/VS) is the crosstalk. The ADG707 is measured with similar connections.

where.IDS: current forced from S to D

equations.name: Insertion loss
equations.expr: Insertion loss = 20 log10(VOUT with switch / VOUT without switch)

operation.text: With EN high, the binary address picks the closed channel: A3 to A0 choose S1 to S16 on the ADG706, and A2 to A0 choose the pair SxA/SxB on the ADG707, with all zeros selecting channel 1. With EN low no switch is on, whatever the address.
On an address change the old channel opens before the new one closes, so two inputs are never shorted together; the gap is at least 1 ns.
The analog range reaches both supply rails, and each switch conducts both ways, so the parts work as multiplexers or demultiplexers.
The parts are specified at 5 V and 3 V single supply and at ±2.5 V dual supply. On a single supply VSS is grounded at the part.
The address and enable inputs accept TTL and CMOS levels.
Internal diodes clamp A, EN, S and D; an overvoltage on these pins has to be current-limited to 30 mA.
The parts are ESD sensitive; charges up to 4000 V from a body or equipment can damage them despite the on-chip protection.
